scope: independent read-only whole-path investigation after exact-base fix1016
finding: Fix1016 materially reduces generic read and deepcopy work, but the request-local ancestry walk still grows from 15 to 498 history-entry calls as distinct entries grow from 3 to 10. The 0.265-to-1.829-second endpoint measurement fails 1.5x but is confounded by JSON/hash instrumentation.

path.app: shotTimelineDataProvider.ts:1124-1142 creates doc.patch; generated.ts:202-204 POSTs commit with Idempotency-Key
path.runtime: service.py:2447-2461 validates and service.py:2508-2515 creates RequestCommitPort
path.agent: commit.py:1227-1231 reads base/head/history; commit.py:1395-1399 checks reservations and can load historical boundaries
path.port: timeline_commit_port.py:210-216 authorizes and opens history_read_scope; :225-244 walks _ancestor; :257-286 caches only revision closures
path.store: timeline_commit_store.py:501-529 holds input/version/CAS checks; :601-695 verifies accepted graph; :1009-1055 authenticates cache hits; :1083-1132 assembles history

why_15_to_498: Each request has observed/base roots and several provider operations ask for ancestry. _ancestor starts at those roots and walks back until its target; it does not retain a per-request result for a previously visited publication. Store entry values are cached, but cache hits still run membership and _verify_accepted, and each new _ancestor invocation repeats the walk. The measured sequence fits 3,4,5,6,7,8,9,10 distinct entries -> 15,33,63,108,171,255,363,498 calls.

necessary_vs_redundant.necessary: Historical growth itself is required: doc.patch rebasing/reservation checks must authenticate the base/current chain, prior records, revision closures, and exact publication/revision pins. history_read_scope must keep SQL/CAS inputs live through dependent reads.
necessary_vs_redundant.redundant_after_verification: Within one request and one unchanged authenticated read snapshot, revisiting the same publication path through _ancestor is repeated work. Candidate cache entries are detached/authenticated; callers receive deep copies, so reuse of an already verified request-private traversal result is safe only inside those boundaries.
necessary_vs_redundant.not_established: No uninstrumented production endpoint curve was established. Do not infer a required D111b flat curve from D112a baseline equivalence.

safe_reuse_boundaries: same RequestCommitPort/request, project/timeline, exact publication/revision pair, and same authenticated history-read scope
retain per-public-call authorization and active/archived membership checks
retain _HistoryReadInputs checks, store-version checks, CAS byte/hash checks, and _verify_accepted live row/ledger/replay validation
invalidate on acceptance writes, unrelated transaction changes, rollback/refusal, close/restart, version or DB/WAL/CAS changes, or failed verification
never carry proofs across requests or bypass revocation/mutation checks
d94_comparison: D94 warm is repeated history-only GET after accepted/restarted state: 27 SQL and zero digest/decode work across N=3..22. D111b is the App POST -> Runtime -> Agent commit lifecycle plus ancestry/reservation reads and canonical readback, so D94 does not validate or invalidate this native whole-path curve.
controls: Prior 123/132/53/2/7 controls and the separate strict 39+1 parent-failure scope are retained and not re-executed. Native XML is absent; raw exit/log is retained and no XML was synthesized.
handback: Bounded remaining cost/missing measurement is request-local repeated ancestry traversal plus the lack of a clean uninstrumented split between provider, port/store reads, and HTTP/canonical readback. No second diagnostic round or implementation change was performed.
